ca_goblin_boulder.blurb: Goblin Boulder is one of the larger blocks on Goblin Hillside, in the Hidden Springs part of Box Springs Mountain Reserve in Riverside. It has eight problems, nearly all between VB and V1 with a single V3, so it suits climbers who want tall but approachable lines or are trying their first highballs. The granite gives a mix of crimps, jugs and flat edges, with xenoliths dotted through it. The ground below is mostly flat but falls away toward the right side of the boulder, and the problems get harder or more committing as you move right. Walk off either side, depending on where you top out.

ca_backyard_the.blurb: The Backyard is a short crag on the Sandals Hillside side of Box Springs Mountain Reserve in Riverside, with eight routes that mix sport, trad and top rope. Grades run from 5.6 to 5.12, with most of the routes between 5.8 and 5.10. The granite is of good quality, and the lines are short crack and face climbs. The wall stands on the left side of a small canyon about halfway up the slope, reached by a trail that leaves from behind a church and heads left. There are no trees at the base, and houses sit nearby, so keep voices down. Top out and either rappel or scramble down to the right.

ca_bald_mountain.blurb: Bald Mountain rises about five miles east of Shaver Lake, with its summit near 7,560 feet and plenty of exposed bedrock around the top. The eight routes are mostly trad, plus a couple of sport lines and a top rope, and the grades span 5.2 to 5.11. Most of them fall around 5.10. A cluster of short bolted climbs sits at Trundle Bay on the west side. Routes are reached by descending from a few hundred feet below the summit on the side you want, and because the summit is a popular lookout, loose rock can fall from above, especially at Trundle Bay.

ca_bandit_buttress.blurb: Bandit Buttress is part of Deadwood Crags in Woodfords Canyon, along Highway 88 south of Lake Tahoe. It holds eight routes, five of them sport, two trad and one top rope, from 5.7 up to 5.11. That makes it a handy stop for climbers working through the moderate grades. The rock is solid and the face looks south, so it is sunny and pleasant on winter days, with snow clearing fast after a storm, while summer afternoons turn hot. The base of the buttress is reached by a well-used trail that climbs from the road.

ca_4_second_alcove.blurb: Second Alcove is a section of The Fortress in Woodfords Canyon near Lake Tahoe, just east of the Donnie G wall. It has eight problems and routes, seven of them trad and one a boulder problem. Most of the trad lines are cracks in the 5.9 to 5.10 range, from thin splitters to wide fist cracks, with one 5.11 as the top end. The granodiorite faces in different directions, so you can pick sun or shade at any hour. A climber's path through the brush leads in to the base of the routes.

ca_av_the_mojo_tooth_area.blurb: The Mojo Tooth Area is a small cliff in the Lower Merced River Canyon, on the north side of the river inside Yosemite National Park, between Five and Dime Cliff and Highway Star. It has eight short routes, mostly trad with a pair of sport lines, ranging from 5.8 up to 5.11. Roughly half of them sit in the 5.10 range and most of the rest in the 5.11 range, so it works for climbers already comfortable on 5.10. The granite cliff is a short distance above a lot at the junction of Highways 140 and 120.
